key_facts: **Clear cell acanthoma** is a rare benign epidermal tumour: a moist red dome-shaped papule, usually on the leg.
Middle-aged and older adults; slowly growing, often under 2 cm.
Dermoscopy is characteristic: dotted vessels in a **'string of pearls'** network.
Differentials: pyogenic granuloma, amelanotic melanoma, BCC, Bowen's disease: biopsy if unsure.
Excision, curettage or cryotherapy if troublesome.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: A rare benign epidermal tumour (Degos acanthoma) made of pale, glycogen-rich keratinocytes. Some regard it as a reactive inflammatory dermatosis rather than a true neoplasm.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Unknown. It often occurs on legs with venous stasis or chronic inflammation. Histology shows sharply demarcated psoriasiform acanthosis of PAS-positive pale cells, with neutrophils in the epidermis.

ul: **"Red papules on the leg are always harmless"**: amelanotic melanoma can look similar.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: A localised patch of **glycogen-rich pale keratinocytes** thickens the epidermis.

mech.t: Keratinocytes accumulate glycogen and look clear.
The epidermis thickens with dilated capillaries in dermal papillae.
Capillaries line up in a reticular necklace pattern.
mech.caption: Dermoscopy: dotted vessels in a 'string of pearls'.

histo: Sharply demarcated psoriasiform acanthosis of pale, PAS-positive keratinocytes, with neutrophils.

sections.title: Clinical features
blocks: A solitary, slowly growing, **moist red-brown dome-shaped papule/nodule (5–20 mm)** on the **lower leg** of a middle-aged/older adult, often with a peripheral collarette of scale. It can bleed. Multiple forms are rare.

variants.name: Collarette
variants.t: Scaly rim on hairy leg. *Site: Leg.*

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: **Dermoscopy:** dotted/glomerular vessels in a **"string of pearls"** (necklace/reticular) arrangement. This is highly characteristic. Confirm with biopsy if there is doubt.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses

ddx.name: Amelanotic melanoma
ddx.f: Pink lesion you can’t name confidently.

blocks: Amelanotic melanoma; Bowen's disease (glomerular vessels in clusters, not strings); psoriasis plaque; pyogenic granuloma; BCC; dermatofibroma; irritated SK; eccrine poroma.

sections.title: Management
blocks: Refer routinely to confirm (the differential includes amelanotic melanoma and Bowen's). Treatment (specialist/GP surgeon): excision, curettage, cryotherapy. Recurrence is uncommon.

ladder.t: **Routine** referral to confirm (differential includes amelanotic melanoma and Bowen’s).
Excision, curettage or cryotherapy; recurrence uncommon.

blocks.title: Prescribing limits and pitfalls
list: **Don’t escalate steroid**: A solitary red scaly leg papule not responding to emollient / steroid isn’t necessarily eczema.

refer.t: Pink lesion you **cannot confidently name**: exclude **amelanotic melanoma**.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Pink lesion you cannot confidently name: refer, as **amelanotic melanoma** must be excluded.

pearls: A red, scaly leg papule that does not respond to emollient/steroid is not necessarily eczema or psoriasis. Look for a solitary lesion and **refer it for dermoscopy/biopsy** rather than escalating steroid potency.
